- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## Bug Report

### 1. Critical — Full table scan in `getUsersById` (`collaboration.ts:32`)

Missing `.where(inArray(appUsers.id, unique))`. Every call to any collaboration endpoint loads the entire users table into memory.

```ts
const rows = await db.select().from(appUsers).where(inArray(appUsers.id, unique));
```
(Also needs `inArray` imported from `drizzle-orm`.)

---

### 2. Critical — No role guard on project creation (`workspaces.ts:344-371`)

`POST /workspaces/:slug/projects` uses `loadWorkspace` which only checks that the user *has any access* (sets role as `"viewer"` if no explicit role). There is no `owner/admin` check like every other write route has (lines 177, 199, 266 all have the check). Any workspace member or viewer can create projects.

**Fix:** Add before the insert:
```ts
if (!["owner", "admin"].includes(req.workspaceRole ?? "") && req.appUserRole !== "admin") {
  res.status(403).json({ error: "Forbidden" });
  return;
}
```

---

### 3. High — `undefined` injected into typed array on batch error (`batch/utils.ts:108`)

```ts
results.push(undefined as R);  // type assertion hides a real undefined
```
When a batch item errors out in `batchProcessWithSSE`, `undefined` is cast to `R` and pushed into `results`. All callers assume the array only contains valid `R` values.

**Fix:** Either filter at the end (`return results.filter((r) => r !== undefined) as R[]`), or change the return type to `(R | undefined)[]` so callers know to handle gaps.

---

### 4. Medium — `balanceScore` goes `NaN` if a stat series is single-entity with value `0` (`balance.ts:72-73`)

```ts
const mean = vals.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / vals.length;  // can be 0
if (mean !== 0 && spread / Math.abs(mean) > 1.5) balanceScore -= 8;
```
This is actually safe for the `spread/mean` division (guarded by `mean !== 0`), but `Math.max(...vals)` / `Math.min(...vals)` on an empty spread array would produce `±Infinity`. const projectId = parseInt(paramAsString(req.params.projectId) || "0", 10);

**Fix:** Check `projectId <= 0 || Number.isNaN(projectId)`.

Here's what I'd change, organized by priority:

---

## Security (fix first)

**Predictable share tokens** (`playtest.ts:139`)
The share token is `sha256("gameforge-feedback-${project.id}").slice(0, 16)` — deterministic, meaning anyone can predict the token for any project ID. Should be a cryptographically random value stored in the DB.

**Missing project access checks** (`collaboration.ts:129`, `collaboration.ts:351`)
Comment creation and version creation only check that the user is logged in, not that they have access to the specific project. Any authenticated user can comment on or create versions for any project they can guess the ID of.

**Weak email validation** (`workspaces.ts:265`)
Workspace invite checks `!email.includes("@")` — that's it. A proper validator would catch garbage inputs, and there's no rate limiting to prevent invite spam.

---

## Performance

**N+1 queries in collaboration** (`collaboration.ts:96`, `collaboration.ts:299`)
Comments and activity feed both load data, then call `getUsersById()` separately. Both should use a JOIN instead of two round-trips.

**No pagination anywhere**
`/projects`, `/chat`, `/research`, `/comments` — all load unbounded rows. As data grows these will become slow and expensive. Every list endpoint needs a `limit`/`offset` or cursor.

**AI clients rebuilt per request** (`aiRouter.ts:158`)
`resolveClients()` instantiates new SDK client objects on every request. These should be cached per API key.

---

## Code Quality

**Massive route handlers**
`workspaces.ts:407-602` is 195 lines in one route. `rules.ts:140-239` is similar. The AI prompt building, JSON parsing, validation, and DB transaction should each be their own function.

**Duplicated AI generation pattern**
`entities.ts`, `rules.ts`, `notes.ts`, `properties.ts`, `players.ts` all do the same thing: call AI → `tryParseJsonArray` → map/truncate → insert. This is 5 copies of the same shape. A helper like `generateAndInsert(prompt, schema, transform)` would cut this significantly.

**Duplicated Zod parse + 400 response**
Almost every route starts with:
```ts
const params = schemas.X.safeParse(req.params);
if (!params.success) { res.status(400).json(...); return; }
```
A small middleware wrapper (`validateParams`, `validateBody`) would remove this from ~25 places.

**`useCollaboration` creates duplicate Y.Doc instances** (`use-collaboration.ts`)
`useCollaboration` and `useSharedText` each create their own `Y.Doc`. They should share one doc per project or you get conflicting document state.

---

## Missing Features

**No rate limiting on AI endpoints**
AI generation calls are expensive and unbounded. A simple per-user/per-workspace limit (e.g. `express-rate-limit`) on `/generate`, `/chat`, `/enhance-*` routes would prevent abuse.

**No soft deletes**
Every delete is hard. Deleting a user orphans their projects. Deleting a rule or entity is irreversible. At minimum, projects and users should have a `deletedAt` column.

**Invitations send no notification** (`workspaces.ts:265-311`)
Workspace invitations are written to the DB but nothing is sent to the invitee — no email, no in-app notification. Users are invited silently.

**`logChange()` silently swallows errors** (`changelog.ts:12-26`)
The function has a bare `catch {}`. If changelog writes fail, nothing tells the caller. Should at least log the error.

**`AiProviderDisabledError` never caught** (`workspaceAiSettings.ts:13`)
The error has `status = 503` on it, but no route catches it to send a 503 — it bubbles up as a 500.

---

## Architecture

**No service layer**
All routes call `db.insert/select/update/delete` directly. There's no separation between HTTP handling and data logic, which makes the routes hard to test and the data logic impossible to reuse.

**User upsert inline in middleware** (`app.ts:45-111`)
66 lines of user-sync business logic lives in the auth middleware. That belongs in a `UserService` or at least a standalone function.

**`tryParseJsonArray`/`tryParseJsonObject` have no shape validation**
They parse to `T` via type assertion with no runtime check that the JSON actually matches `T`. Zod schemas already exist for everything — these should validate against them instead of blind-casting.

---

## What I'd tackle in order

1. Predictable share tokens (security, one-liner fix)
2. Missing project access checks on collaboration routes (security)
3. Pagination on the main list endpoints (correctness before scale)
4. Rate limiting on AI routes (prevent abuse)
5. Extract the duplicated Zod-parse pattern into middleware (quality, biggest return on smallest effort)
6. Split the large route handlers into functions (quality)
7. Fix `AiProviderDisabledError` propagation (correctness)
8. Soft deletes on projects/users (data safety)

1	import { Router, type IRouter } from "express";
2	import { desc, sql, isNotNull, eq, inArray } from "drizzle-orm";
3	import {
4	  db,
5	  projects,
6	  entities,
7	  rules,
8	  chatMessages,
9	} from "@workspace/db";
10	import { schemas } from "@workspace/api-zod";
11	import { requireAuth } from "../middlewares/projectAuth";
12	
13	const router: IRouter = Router();
14	
15	router.use("/dashboard", requireAuth);
16	
17	async function visibleProjectIds(
18	  userId: number | undefined,
19	  isAdmin: boolean,
20	): Promise<number[]> {
21	  if (isAdmin) {
22	    const all = await db.select({ id: projects.id }).from(projects);
23	    return all.map((p) => p.id);
24	  }
25	  if (!userId) return [];
26	  const own = await db
27	    .select({ id: projects.id })
28	    .from(projects)
29	    .where(eq(projects.ownerUserId, userId));
30	  return own.map((p) => p.id);
31	}
32	
33	router.get("/dashboard/summary", async (req, res): Promise<void> => {
34	  const isAdmin = req.appUserRole === "admin";
35	  const ids = await visibleProjectIds(req.appUserId, isAdmin);
36	
37	  if (ids.length === 0) {
38	    res.json(
39	      schemas.GetDashboardSummaryResponse.parse({
40	        projectCount: 0,
41	        entityCount: 0,
42	        ruleCount: 0,
43	        chatMessageCount: 0,
44	        gameTypeBreakdown: [],
45	        genreBreakdown: [],
46	      }),
47	    );
48	    return;
49	  }
50	
51	  const [{ projectCount }] = await db
52	    .select({ projectCount: sql<number>`count(*)::int` })
53	    .from(projects)
54	    .where(inArray(projects.id, ids));
55	  const [{ entityCount }] = await db
56	    .select({ entityCount: sql<number>`count(*)::int` })
57	    .from(entities)
58	    .where(inArray(entities.projectId, ids));
59	  const [{ ruleCount }] = await db
60	    .select({ ruleCount: sql<number>`count(*)::int` })
61	    .from(rules)
62	    .where(inArray(rules.projectId, ids));
63	  const [{ chatMessageCount }] = await db
64	    .select({ chatMessageCount: sql<number>`count(*)::int` })
65	    .from(chatMessages)
66	    .where(inArray(chatMessages.projectId, ids));
67	
68	  const gameTypeBreakdown = await db
69	    .select({
70	      gameType: sql<string>`${projects.gameType}`,
71	      count: sql<number>`count(*)::int`,
72	    })
73	    .from(projects)
74	    .where(sql`${isNotNull(projects.gameType)} AND ${inArray(projects.id, ids)}`)
75	    .groupBy(projects.gameType)
76	    .orderBy(desc(sql`count(*)`));
77	
78	  const genreBreakdown = await db
79	    .select({
80	      genre: sql<string>`${projects.genre}`,
81	      count: sql<number>`count(*)::int`,
82	    })
83	    .from(projects)
84	    .where(sql`${isNotNull(projects.genre)} AND ${inArray(projects.id, ids)}`)
85	    .groupBy(projects.genre)
86	    .orderBy(desc(sql`count(*)`));
87	
88	  res.json(
89	    schemas.GetDashboardSummaryResponse.parse({
90	      projectCount,
91	      entityCount,
92	      ruleCount,
93	      chatMessageCount,
94	      gameTypeBreakdown,
95	      genreBreakdown,
96	    }),
97	  );
98	});
99	
100	router.get("/dashboard/recent-activity", async (req, res): Promise<void> => {
101	  const isAdmin = req.appUserRole === "admin";
102	  const ids = await visibleProjectIds(req.appUserId, isAdmin);
103	  if (ids.length === 0) {
104	    res.json(schemas.GetRecentActivityResponse.parse([]));
105	    return;
106	  }
107	
108	  const limit = 20;
109	  const projectRows = await db
110	    .select({
111	      id: projects.id,
112	      name: projects.name,
113	      createdAt: projects.createdAt,
114	    })
115	    .from(projects)
116	    .where(inArray(projects.id, ids))
117	    .orderBy(desc(projects.createdAt))
118	    .limit(limit);
119	
120	  const entityRows = await db
121	    .select({
122	      id: entities.id,
123	      projectId: entities.projectId,
124	      name: entities.name,
125	      createdAt: entities.createdAt,
126	      projectName: projects.name,
127	    })
128	    .from(entities)
129	    .innerJoin(projects, eq(projects.id, entities.projectId))
130	    .where(inArray(entities.projectId, ids))
131	    .orderBy(desc(entities.createdAt))
132	    .limit(limit);
133	
134	  const ruleRows = await db
135	    .select({
136	      id: rules.id,
137	      projectId: rules.projectId,
138	      title: rules.title,
139	      createdAt: rules.createdAt,
140	      projectName: projects.name,
141	    })
142	    .from(rules)
143	    .innerJoin(projects, eq(projects.id, rules.projectId))
144	    .where(inArray(rules.projectId, ids))
145	    .orderBy(desc(rules.createdAt))
146	    .limit(limit);
147	
148	  const chatRows = await db
149	    .select({
150	      id: chatMessages.id,
151	      projectId: chatMessages.projectId,
152	      content: chatMessages.content,
153	      role: chatMessages.role,
154	      createdAt: chatMessages.createdAt,
155	      projectName: projects.name,
156	    })
157	    .from(chatMessages)
158	    .innerJoin(projects, eq(projects.id, chatMessages.projectId))
159	    .where(inArray(chatMessages.projectId, ids))
160	    .orderBy(desc(chatMessages.createdAt))
161	    .limit(limit);
162	
163	  const events = [
164	    ...projectRows.map((p) => ({
165	      id: `project-${p.id}`,
166	      projectId: p.id,
167	      projectName: p.name,
168	      kind: "project_created",
169	      title: `Project created: ${p.name}`,
170	      createdAt: p.createdAt,
171	    })),
172	    ...entityRows.map((e) => ({
173	      id: `entity-${e.id}`,
174	      projectId: e.projectId,
175	      projectName: e.projectName,
176	      kind: "entity_added",
177	      title: `Entity added: ${e.name}`,
178	      createdAt: e.createdAt,
179	    })),
180	    ...ruleRows.map((r) => ({
181	      id: `rule-${r.id}`,
182	      projectId: r.projectId,
183	      projectName: r.projectName,
184	      kind: "rule_added",
185	      title: `Rule added: ${r.title}`,
186	      createdAt: r.createdAt,
187	    })),
188	    ...chatRows.map((c) => ({
189	      id: `chat-${c.id}`,
190	      projectId: c.projectId,
191	      projectName: c.projectName,
192	      kind: c.role === "assistant" ? "assistant_reply" : "user_message",
193	      title:
194	        c.role === "assistant"
195	          ? `AI replied in ${c.projectName}`
196	          : `You asked: ${c.content.slice(0, 80)}${c.content.length > 80 ? "…" : ""}`,
197	      createdAt: c.createdAt,
198	    })),
199	  ]
200	    .sort((a, b) => b.createdAt.getTime() - a.createdAt.getTime())
201	    .slice(0, limit);
202	
203	  res.json(schemas.GetRecentActivityResponse.parse(events));
204	});

### Backend — 4 new routes (`workspaces.ts`)

| Method | Path | Auth | What it does |
|--------|------|------|--------------|
| `GET` | `/workspaces/join/:code` | None | Returns workspace name + member count for preview. Safe to call before login. |
| `POST` | `/workspaces/join/:code` | Required | Adds the caller as a `member` of the workspace. Re-joining is safe (upsert). |
| `GET` | `/workspaces/:slug/invite-code` | Owner/Admin | Returns the join URL. Lazily generates a code on first call. |
| `POST` | `/workspaces/:slug/invite-code/refresh` | Owner/Admin | Generates a new code, invalidating the old link immediately. |

### Frontend

**`MembersDialog`** — owners/admins now see an invite link section at the top:
- Displays the full `yourapp.com/join/...` URL
- **Copy** button with a checkmark confirmation
- **Refresh** button (resets the link, old one stops working)

**`/join/:code` page** (`join-workspace.tsx`) — the link destination:
- Loads without auth, shows workspace name and member count
- Unauthenticated users see "Sign in to join" and "Create account" buttons that redirect back after login
- Authenticated users see a single "Join [Workspace Name]" button
- On success: shows a green checkmark and redirects to the workspace automatically

### How it works end to end
1. Owner opens **Members** → copies the invite link
2. Sends it to anyone (Slack, email, etc.)
3. Recipient opens the link, sees the workspace name and current member count
4. They sign in if needed (redirected back), then click **Join**
5. They land directly inside the workspace and can see all its projects
